oral_prep_visits_per_year.notes: Standard monitoring visits per MDR PrEP Nederland v4.5 (July 2025): 6-monthly consultations = 2 visits/year. 3-monthly visits are optional via shared decision-making for higher-risk individuals (sensitivity scenario only). Updated from outdated 4 visits/year (old MDR 2022 quarterly assumption).

hiv_art_visits_per_year.notes: HIV-positive individuals on ART are assigned quarterly outpatient monitoring visits (viral load/labs/clinical review) in the societal patient-time component. This is applied equally across arms and only differs through the number of HIV-positive on-ART patients.

components.sti_bundle_includes: Chlamydia NAAT x3 sites + Gonorrhoea NAAT x3 sites + Syphilis TPHA + HIV 4th gen Ag/Ab combo + order tariff

shared.notes: MDR PrEP Nederland v4.5 (July 2025) standard monitoring: 2 consultations/year (6-monthly). Per consultation: outpatient visit EUR 120 (iMTA 2024) + full STI lab bundle EUR 307.25 (NZA 2025 tariffs). Annual total: 2 x (EUR 120 + EUR 307.25) = EUR 854.50. Applies identically to both arms. PROTOCOL NOTE: Prior Dutch PrEP standard (MDR PrEP v3/v4, 2022) specified quarterly monitoring (4 visits/year = EUR 1,709/year). MDR v4.5 (July 2025) updated this to 6-monthly as the standard interval, with quarterly visits retained as an option under shared decision-making for higher-risk individuals. This model uses the v4.5 standard (2 visits/year); quarterly monitoring may be evaluated as a sensitivity scenario.
shared.source: MDR PrEP Nederland v4.5 July 2025 (monitoring interval). Hakkaart-van Roijen et al. (2024) iMTA Costing Manual Appendix 1 (outpatient EUR 120). NZA maximumtarieven diagnostiek 2025 (codes 70003 EUR 40.86/site, 70626 EUR 12.21, 71118 EUR 15.02, 71144 EUR 26.97, 79989 EUR 7.89).

shared.label: Renal function monitoring (creatinine) — oral PrEP users only
shared.notes: TDF-based oral PrEP requires renal function monitoring per MDR PrEP v4.5. 2 creatinine tests/year x NZA code 70419 (EUR 2.13) = EUR 4.26/year. Not applicable to lenacapavir (no TDF component). Included for methodological completeness; negligible budget impact.
shared.source: MDR PrEP Nederland v4.5 July 2025. NZA maximumtarieven diagnostiek 2025 code 70419 (creatinine EUR 2.13).

adverse_events.notes: Base case uses prevalence mode. Oral PrEP GI/renal AE cost and disutility items were removed from the base case on 2026-05-22. iPrEx reported more nausea during the first four weeks but similar serious-adverse-event rates; PROUD reported no serious adverse drug reactions, although 28 adverse-event episodes interrupted PrEP and 20/21 affected participants restarted; IPERGAY reported similar serious-adverse-event rates but higher GI (14% vs 5%) and renal (18% vs 10%) adverse-event rates with TDF/FTC. These trials support a generally manageable safety profile but do not directly establish zero incremental QALY or cost. The zero oral-PrEP AE decrement/cost is therefore a weakly supported base-case structural assumption, not an empirical finding. Oral renal monitoring remains included under prevention_costs.shared.prep_renal_monitoring_oral. Lenacapavir ISR/nodule utility burden remains included.

items.label: Transient injection site reactions — Lenacapavir ongoing

state_machine_params._notes: resolution_rate_per_year=6.0 implies mean resolution ~2 months, appropriate for transient ISRs (redness, swelling, pain). State-machine params inactive in prevalence mode.

prevalence.notes: Transient ISR prevalence = total ISR prevalence (0.760) minus persistent nodule prevalence (0.355). Non-overlapping split: this item covers patients with ISRs that resolve, excluding persistent non-resolving nodules. Total ISR prevalence 0.760 is midpoint of PURPOSE-1 (68.8%) and PURPOSE-2 (83.2%). No direct CI is reported for the derived transient fraction; beta distribution is approximate and should be complemented by deterministic sensitivity analysis.
prevalence.source: EMA CHMP Assessment Report, Yeytuo (lenacapavir), EMA/265754/2025, Table 63 and safety section. PURPOSE-1: 68.8% any ISR; PURPOSE-2: 83.2% any ISR.

distribution._notes: Beta(40,59): mean=0.404, SD~0.049. Approximate — derived value, no direct trial CI.

utility_decrement.notes: Proxy-sourced utility loss for transient ISR. PURPOSE/EPAR provides lenacapavir-specific prevalence but no EQ-5D utility decrement. NICE TA1106 cabotegravir PrEP EAG scenario EAG 05 assumed an ISR disutility of -0.015 applied per cycle. We split that average burden into -0.01 for transient ISRs and -0.02 for persistent nodules; weighted by current prevalence (0.405 transient, 0.355 persistent), the mean decrement among ISR/nodule cases is -0.0147, approximately matching TA1106. Use sensitivity analysis around this proxy because it is cabotegravir-derived, not lenacapavir-specific.
utility_decrement.source: NICE TA1106 Cabotegravir for preventing HIV-1, committee papers, EAG 05: per-cycle ISR costs and disutility; EMA CHMP Assessment Report Yeytuo (lenacapavir), EMA/265754/2025 for lenacapavir ISR prevalence.

cost.notes: Base-case assumption: no incremental medical management cost for transient lenacapavir injection-site reactions. This follows a conservative cabotegravir-style costing approach in which mild ISRs are not costed and any treatment resource use is negligible. Utility decrement captures patient burden; medical-management costs can be added as a sensitivity if treatment-seeking evidence is identified.
cost.source: Model assumption informed by NICE cabotegravir PrEP appraisal structure; no Dutch lenacapavir-specific ISR treatment-cost evidence identified.

items.label: Persistent injection site nodule — Lenacapavir ongoing

state_machine_params._notes: resolution_rate_per_year=0.5 derived from EPAR: ~35-36% of LEN users had non-resolving nodules at end of observation (~2 years). Solving 1-exp(-r*2)=0.64 gives r~0.51. Inactive in prevalence mode.

prevalence.notes: Non-resolving injection-site nodule/induration prevalence among lenacapavir users. Midpoint of PURPOSE-1 and PURPOSE-2 end-of-observation rates (both approximately 35-36%), reported consistently across both trials. This is a subset of the total ISR population and is not double counted with transient ISR. No formal 95% CI was reported in the EPAR; beta distribution is approximate and should be complemented by deterministic sensitivity analysis [0.25, 0.45].
prevalence.source: EMA CHMP Assessment Report, Yeytuo (lenacapavir), EMA/265754/2025, safety section. PURPOSE-1 LEN arm: ~35-36% non-resolving nodule at end of observation. PURPOSE-2 LEN arm: ~35-36% non-resolving nodule at end of observation.

distribution._notes: Beta(90,163): mean=0.356, SD~0.030. Approximate — no direct CI from EPAR. Parameterised assuming SD=0.03 (reflecting uncertainty in the absence of CI). Sensitivity analysis should test wide range [0.25, 0.45].

utility_decrement.notes: Proxy-sourced utility loss for persistent injection-site nodule. PURPOSE/EPAR provides lenacapavir-specific persistent nodule prevalence but no EQ-5D utility decrement. NICE TA1106 cabotegravir PrEP EAG scenario EAG 05 assumed an ISR disutility of -0.015 applied per cycle. We assign a larger decrement to persistent nodules (-0.02) than transient ISRs (-0.01) to reflect longer duration/cosmetic burden while preserving the NICE average: weighted by prevalence (0.405 transient, 0.355 persistent), mean decrement among ISR/nodule cases is -0.0147. Use sensitivity analysis because this is a cabotegravir-derived proxy and persistent nodule-specific utility evidence is unavailable.
utility_decrement.source: NICE TA1106 Cabotegravir for preventing HIV-1, committee papers, EAG 05: per-cycle ISR costs and disutility; EMA CHMP Assessment Report Yeytuo (lenacapavir), EMA/265754/2025 for lenacapavir persistent nodule prevalence.

distribution._notes: Wide uninformative prior pending literature sourcing.

cost.notes: Base-case assumption: persistent injection-site nodules are not assigned incremental treatment costs because routine medical treatment/removal is not established. Patient burden is represented through utility decrement only. Dermatology or removal costs should be tested only as a sensitivity if treatment-seeking evidence is identified.
cost.source: Model assumption informed by NICE cabotegravir PrEP appraisal structure; no Dutch lenacapavir-specific persistent-nodule treatment-cost evidence identified.

adverse_events._oral_prep_ae_exclusion_note: Removed oral_prep_initiation_renal_screen, oral_prep_gi_ae, and oral_prep_renal_ae from base-case AE items on 2026-05-22. Renal screening/monitoring is costed in prevention_costs rather than adverse_events; oral PrEP GI/renal toxicity is not assigned a separate base-case cost or disutility. Evidence: iPrEx — Grant RM et al. N Engl J Med. 2010;363:2587-2599. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1011205, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21091279/ (more nausea during first 4 weeks; similar serious-adverse-event rates); PROUD — McCormack S et al. Lancet. 2016;387:53-60. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(15)00056-2, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26364263/ (no serious adverse drug reactions; 28 interruption-causing adverse-event episodes, 20/21 restarted); IPERGAY — Molina JM et al. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:2237-2246. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1506273, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26624850/ (similar serious-adverse-event rates but GI 14% vs 5% and renal 18% vs 10%). Evidence status: weakly supported for assigning exactly zero incremental QALY/cost because none of these trials directly estimated that economic quantity; the zero is a base-case structural assumption.

health_effects_rate.notes: ZIN guideline: 1.5% annual discount rate for health effects

cost_rate.notes: ZIN guideline: 4.0% annual discount rate for costs

susceptible.notes: Full health utility for HIV-negative individuals not on PrEP. Convention used in Dutch PrEP CEA (Nichols 2016) and NICE TA1106 (2025).
susceptible.source: Convention: Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423); NICE TA1106 2025

susceptible_oral_prep.notes: No EQ-5D evidence for PrEP utility decrement. Nichols 2016 Dutch PrEP CEA and NICE TA1106 both apply zero decrement for PrEP use. Previous value of 0.99 was clinical judgment with no source.
susceptible_oral_prep.source: Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423, Table S1); NICE TA1106 2025 (no PrEP decrement applied)

susceptible_lenacapavir.notes: No EQ-5D evidence for lenacapavir PrEP utility decrement. Same convention as oral PrEP. Previous differential (0.005) vs oral PrEP was unsourced and created a structural QALY advantage for lenacapavir without evidence.
susceptible_lenacapavir.source: Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423, Table S1); NICE TA1106 2025 (no PrEP decrement applied)

hiv_acute.notes: Proxy for early/acute HIV (symptomatic, CD4 200-350). Tengs & Lin 2002 pooled TTO symptomatic HIV = 0.82; Nichols 2016 Dutch CEA Table S1 CD4 200-350 = 0.82. Value 0.78 is midpoint between symptomatic HIV (0.82) and AIDS (0.70) to reflect acute phase severity. Previous value 0.70 was the Tengs AIDS estimate, not acute HIV.
hiv_acute.source: Tengs & Lin 2002 (Med Decis Making 22:475, Table 2 TTO patient pooled); Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423, Table S1 CD4 200-350)

bounds.upper_source: Nichols 2016 Table S1 CD4>350 sensitivity value

hiv_chronic_on_art.notes: Stable chronic HIV on suppressive ART, expressed on the model convention where susceptible/no HIV utility is 1.0. Popping 2021 reports Dutch PLHIV EQ-5D-5L utility 0.850 and Dutch general-population utility 0.869; the normalized model-scale value is 0.850/0.869 = 0.978, rounded to 0.98. This replaces direct use of 0.850, which mixed an absolute population utility with a susceptible state fixed at 1.0.
hiv_chronic_on_art.source: Popping et al. 2021 (Lancet Reg Health Eur 8:100177; NL n=895, EQ-5D-5L, Versteegh 2016 NL tariff)

bounds.lower_source: Popping 2021 absolute Dutch PLHIV EQ-5D-5L utility, conservative unnormalised sensitivity

hiv_chronic_off_art.notes: Chronic HIV off ART: CD4 decline without treatment. Value 0.78 is consistent with Tengs & Lin 2002 symptomatic HIV and Nichols 2016 CD4 200-350 (0.82), adjusted downward to reflect off-ART status. Miners 2014 stopped-ART disutility −0.18 vs NL norm 0.85 gives 0.67 as lower bound.
hiv_chronic_off_art.source: Tengs & Lin 2002 (Med Decis Making 22:475, Table 2, symptomatic HIV 0.82 proxy); Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423, Table S1 CD4 200-350 = 0.82)

bounds.lower_source: Miners et al. 2014 stopped-ART disutility −0.18 applied to NL norm 0.85
bounds.upper_source: NL EQ-5D-5L population norm (Versteegh 2016; Popping 2021 = 0.869, rounded to 0.85 for 3L comparability)

aids_on_art.notes: AIDS-stage on ART after applying the late-presenter initiation penalty. Set equal to stable chronic ART because the expected five-year recovery loss is charged once through utility_decrements.late_presenter_art_initiation. This avoids permanently penalising AIDS-on-ART person-time in a model that does not track immune-recovery tunnel states.
aids_on_art.source: Popping et al. 2021 (Lancet Reg Health Eur 8:100177; NL PLHIV utility 0.850); Popping et al. 2023 (PLoS ONE 18:e0280877; late/very-late presentation costs persist through 5 years); Tengs & Lin 2002 / Nichols 2016 untreated AIDS utility anchor 0.70

bounds.lower_source: Popping 2021 absolute Dutch PLHIV EQ-5D-5L utility, conservative unnormalised sensitivity
bounds.upper_source: Model susceptible/no-HIV convention and linked chronic-on-ART upper bound

aids_off_art.notes: AIDS off ART. Tengs & Lin 2002 provides a single pooled AIDS utility (0.70) with no ART stratification; Nichols 2016 uses the same AIDS-stage base value. In the current HTA utility structure this remains the untreated AIDS anchor, while late-presenter ART morbidity is represented by a one-time ART-initiation utility decrement. Previous value 0.40 had no literature source and was below all published estimates.
aids_off_art.source: Tengs & Lin 2002 (Med Decis Making 22:475, Table 2, AIDS TTO patient pooled 0.702); Nichols et al. 2016 (Lancet Infect Dis 16:1423, Table S1 AIDS CD4 <200 = 0.70).

bounds.lower_source: Nichols 2016 Table S1 AIDS sensitivity low
bounds.upper_source: Nichols 2016 Table S1 AIDS sensitivity high

late_presenter_art_initiation.notes: One-time QALY decrement for AIDS-stage late presenters initiating ART. Derived as (stable ART utility 0.98 - late-recovery proxy 0.85) x 5 years = 0.65 QALYs. This decrement is kept undiscounted here because the HTA accumulator applies the model's health discounting when QALYs are accumulated; discounting the parameter itself would risk double discounting under the current event-decrement implementation. Popping 2023 supports persistent excess morbidity/resource use through five years after ART initiation in late and very-late presenters, but does not directly measure utility by presentation timing. Kept fixed in PSA to avoid sampling this derived decrement independently of the underlying utility values.
late_presenter_art_initiation.source: Derived from Popping et al. 2021 Dutch PLHIV utility and Popping et al. 2023 five-year late-presentation cost persistence; Tengs & Lin 2002 / Nichols 2016 AIDS utility anchor for lower-bound context.

bounds.lower_source: No additional late-presenter utility penalty sensitivity

wtp_threshold_eur_per_qaly.notes: WTP threshold per QALY for HIV/AIDS under ZIN proportional shortfall scale. Diseases with proportional shortfall >= 0.70 qualify for tier 3 threshold of EUR 80,000/QALY. HIV/AIDS qualifies given substantial life-years lost relative to healthy life expectancy.
wtp_threshold_eur_per_qaly.source: Zorginstituut Nederland (2022). Richtlijn voor economische evaluaties in de gezondheidszorg. https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/publicaties/rapport/2022/08/15/richtlijn-voor-economische-evaluaties-in-de-gezondheidszorg

art_first_line.notes: Annual cost of first-line ART. Adjusted-config base case uses Dovato 50/300 mg AIP: EUR 4,453.54 per six months x 2 = EUR 8,907/year. Low sensitivity candidate: current model EUR 7,352. High sensitivity candidate: Biktarvy adult 50/200/25 mg AIP EUR 10,651/year.
art_first_line.source: Farmacotherapeutisch Kompas / Zorginstituut Nederland cost overview for Dovato (dolutegravir/lamivudine 50/300 mg).
art_first_line._psa_range_note: Suggested ART price range for sensitivity/PSA: low EUR 7,352; base EUR 8,907; high EUR 10,651.

hiv_monitoring_on_art.notes: Superseded in adjusted config by Popping stage-specific non-ART care cost items below. Set to zero to avoid double-counting.
hiv_monitoring_on_art.source: Superseded by Popping et al. 2023 Table 3 stage-specific non-ART cost items.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_timely_year1.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Timely presentation year-1 cost: EUR 2,407 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 3,133 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; frequency:once charges the year-1 bundle to gross ART initiators in this stage.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_timely_year1.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_timely_maintenance.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Timely presentation years 2-5 annual average: EUR 2,205.75 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 2,871 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; applies to on-ART continuing stock after excluding same-step ART initiators.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_timely_maintenance.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_late_year1.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Late presentation year-1 cost: EUR 4,749 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 6,182 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; frequency:once charges the year-1 bundle to gross ART initiators in this stage. Mapping all Chronic-on-ART to Late is conservative; use Timely for Chronic in a lower-cost sensitivity if desired.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_late_year1.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_late_maintenance.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Late presentation years 2-5 annual average: EUR 3,202.75 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 4,169 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; applies to on-ART continuing stock after excluding same-step ART initiators.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_late_maintenance.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_very_late_year1.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Very late presentation year-1 cost: EUR 15,886 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 20,680 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; frequency:once charges the year-1 bundle to gross ART initiators in this stage. AIDS-off-ART remains covered by aids_hospitalization.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_very_late_year1.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

hiv_non_art_care_tier_very_late_maintena.notes: Adjusted-config Popping non-ART care tier. Very late presentation years 2-5 annual average: EUR 5,743.75 in 2018 EUR, inflated to EUR 7,477 in 2025 EUR using CPI factor 1.3018. Requires V12.18 disease-cost cohort routing; applies to on-ART continuing stock after excluding same-step ART initiators. AIDS-off-ART remains covered by aids_hospitalization.
hiv_non_art_care_tier_very_late_maintena.source: Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877, Table 3; CBS CPI 2019-2025.

aids_hospitalization.notes: Annual cost of AIDS-stage care without ART: opportunistic infection hospitalisations, OI drug treatment, supportive outpatient care. Restricted to off_art only (architecture decision 2026-04-29) — AIDS-on-ART patients are covered by hiv_monitoring_on_art. Value: iMTA 2024 bottom-up construction (1.5 OI episodes x 18 ward days x EUR 644/day + OI drugs + visits ~ EUR 21,868/year). Corroborated by Popping et al. (2023) ATHENA cohort: very late presenter non-ART costs year 1 EUR 15,886 (2018 EUR), inflated to 2025 ~ EUR 20,680 lower bound.
aids_hospitalization.source: Hakkaart-van Roijen et al. (2024) iMTA Costing Manual, Appendix 1 (hospital ward day EUR 644). Popping et al. (2023) PLoS ONE 18(2):e0280877 (ATHENA cohort, very late presenter non-ART costs, 2018 EUR).

hiv_diagnosis_linkage._architecture_note: billing_moment='diagnosis' fires once per person transitioning Undiagnosed→Diagnosed in a given step. The applies_to_stages and applies_to_art_status fields are NOT evaluated for diagnosis-billing items — the accumulator applies the cost directly to the new_diagnoses counter. Those fields have been removed to avoid misleading readers.
hiv_diagnosis_linkage.notes: One-time per-diagnosis linkage bundle, rounded from Dutch guidance/tariffs: reactive HIV screen/antigen EUR 39.66, confirmatory blot EUR 60.01, HIV viral load EUR 113.75, CD4/CD8 EUR 33.04, HIV RNA genotyping or sequence analysis EUR 241.58-257.51, first specialist linkage visit EUR 120, and blood/order handling about EUR 15. Broader STI/baseline screening is not included here to avoid overlap with first-year HIV care bundles. Rounded base-case value EUR 600; use EUR 500-750 as a sensitivity range.
hiv_diagnosis_linkage.source: RIVM LCI HIV-infectie guideline (diagnostic confirmation, HIV-RNA after confirmed positive, referral to HIV treatment centre). NVHB Richtlijn HIV: first consult in people with HIV (documented confirmation/Western blot, HIV-RNA, CD4, resistance testing on indication). GGD Amsterdam Streeklaboratorium 2025 tariffs: 071118 EUR 14.19, 071144 EUR 25.47, 070185 EUR 60.01, 070005 EUR 113.75. NZA maximumtarieven diagnostiek 2025: 70007 DNA/RNA analysis EUR 241.58. Amsterdam UMC ODV 2025/2026: HIV RNA genotyping EUR 257.51; HIV RNA quantitative EUR 116.07. Hakkaart-van Roijen et al. (2024) iMTA Costing Manual Appendix 1 outpatient visit EUR 120.

hiv_terminal_care.notes: Intentionally zero (architecture decision 2026-04-29). Terminal care costs for AIDS-off-ART patients are implicitly captured in the final time-steps of aids_hospitalization (EUR 22,000/year ongoing until death). Adding a separate lump sum at death would double-count the final period. Evidence: Van Dijk et al. (2025) Eur J Health Econ confirms Dutch end-of-life costs concentrate in months t-1 and t-2 before death — the ongoing AIDS state cost already captures this. If a societal terminal care sensitivity is needed in future, size as ~2 months ICU/ward above the ongoing AIDS state cost citing Dijk 2025.
hiv_terminal_care.source: Van Dijk et al. (2025) Eur J Health Econ. DOI: 10.1007/s10198-025-01763-w
